unit.title: Develop and apply principles of professional codes of conduct & ethics

theory1.instructions: Answer all 45 questions. Each question has one best answer: choose it. Each question is worth 1 mark. Time allowed: 2 hours 30 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

questions.stem: What is a code of conduct at work?
options: A secret password staff use to get into the villa
A list of the prices the villa charges for each room
A written set of rules on how staff should behave
A plan showing which staff work on each day of the week

questions.stem: What does "ethics" mean at work?
options: Knowing right from wrong, and choosing to do right
Doing whatever the guest asks, even if it breaks the law
Working as fast as you can to finish before the shift ends
Keeping your opinions to yourself in every staff meeting

questions.stem: Why do villas and hotels have a code of conduct?
options: So managers can punish staff without giving any reason
So staff need no more training once they have started
So guests know how much to tip each member of staff
So every worker knows the behaviour that is expected

questions.stem: You start a new job at a villa. How should you learn its code of conduct?
options: Wait until you break a rule, then ask what the rule was
Read it, ask about anything unclear, and sign for it
Ask one of the guests which rules the staff must follow
Copy whatever the longest-serving worker does each day

questions.stem: The shop gives you too much change when you buy supplies for the villa. What should you do?
options: Give back the extra money and get a correct receipt
Keep the extra, since it was the shop that made the mistake
Share the extra money with the other staff at lunch
Spend it on more supplies without telling anyone

questions.stem: Garfield, a gardener, writes on his time sheet that he worked until 5 p.m., but he left at 3 p.m. What is this?
options: Fine, because all of the work was finished early anyway
Fine, as long as his supervisor did not see him leave
Dishonest, because the villa pays for time not worked
A small matter that does not affect anyone else at all

questions.stem: A guest leaves a half-full bottle of rum in the villa when they check out. What should you do?
options: Take it home, since the guest clearly did not want it
Drink it with the other staff at the end of the shift
Sell it to the next guest who comes to stay at the villa
Hand it in to the supervisor, as the villa's rules say

questions.stem: While cleaning a room after a guest has checked out, you find a gold ring under the bed. What should you do?
options: Keep it in your pocket until the end of your shift
Hand it in at once and record it as lost property
Leave it under the bed in case the guest comes back
Wear it to keep it safe until somebody asks for it

questions.stem: A caller asks which villa a famous singer is staying in. What should you do?
options: Give the villa name, since the caller sounds friendly
Say politely that you cannot give out guest details
Give the details if the caller says they are family
Tell them to drive round the area and look for the car

questions.stem: Why must staff not post photos of guests on social media?
options: Photos of guests use up too much of the phone's data
Guests always look better in professional photographs
Only managers are allowed to have a smartphone at work
It breaks the guest's privacy and the villa's trust

questions.stem: Which guest details should staff keep private?
options: Names, villa, phone numbers and card details
Only card numbers; other details can be shared freely
None, because guest details are public once they book
Only the details that the guest has written down

questions.stem: Two workers talk loudly about a guest's health problem near the pool. What is wrong with this?
options: They ought to be talking about the weather or sport instead
They are not speaking loudly enough to be heard
Private guest details are shared where others can hear
Nothing, as long as that guest is not at the pool

questions.stem: A guest's laptop is open on the table in the villa you are cleaning. What should you do?
options: Close it and carry it to the bedroom to keep it safe
Read the screen to see whether the guest needs help
Clean around it with care, and do not touch or read it
Use it to check your own email while you are on break

questions.stem: When may you enter a guest's bedroom in an occupied villa?
options: When your work needs it, after knocking and saying who you are
Whenever you like, since the villa belongs to your employer
Only at night, when the guests are less likely to see you
When you want to see what the guests have brought with them

questions.stem: A guest offers you a large cash gift. What should you do?
options: Take it quietly and never tell anyone about it
Ask the guest for more, since they can clearly afford it
Refuse rudely, so the guest can see that you are honest
Follow the villa's gift policy and tell your supervisor

questions.stem: A tour operator offers to pay you each time you send villa guests on one of his tours. What is this?
options: A normal bonus that you do not need to mention to anyone
A conflict of interest that you must tell your manager about
A good deal, as long as the tours are not too expensive
Fine, as long as the guests never find out about it

questions.stem: What is a conflict of interest?
options: When two guests want to book the same villa on one date
When you and a colleague argue about the work schedule
When a guest is not interested in the tours on offer
When your own gain could sway a decision you make at work

questions.stem: A guest asks you out on a date after your shift. What is the most professional reply?
options: Agree, but ask the guest not to tell your manager
Give the guest your home address so they can visit
Thank them politely and say staff do not date guests
Laugh at the guest in front of the other guests

questions.stem: Why should staff not give guests their personal phone numbers?
options: Calls between staff and guests are always against the law
It blurs work and private life and can break villa policy
Guests never need to contact any staff for any reason
Personal phones do not work well out in the country

questions.stem: You will be late for your shift because the bus has broken down. What should you do?
options: Call your supervisor as soon as you can and give a time
Say nothing and hope that nobody notices you are late
Stay home for the day, since you will be late anyway
Ask a friend to sign in for you before you get there

questions.stem: Why does punctuality matter in a villa team?
options: Others must cover for you and guests may be kept waiting
The manager likes to see who arrives first each day
It only matters on the days the owner visits the villa
Clocks at work are always faster than those at home

questions.stem: What does your appearance at work show to guests?
options: Nothing, since guests only care about the price
How much money you earn outside of your work
Which school you went to when you were a child
Respect for them and the standard of the villa

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT acceptable behaviour on duty?
options: Greeting guests with a smile when you pass them
Drinking from the guests' bar during your shift
Asking your supervisor when you are not sure
Keeping your phone away while serving guests

questions.stem: Why are drugs and alcohol not allowed while you are at work?
options: They are only banned when the owner is at the villa
They are allowed if you only take a small amount
They affect judgement and safety, putting guests at risk
They are banned only for staff who drive the villa car

questions.stem: What is sexual harassment at work?
options: Any friendly greeting between two colleagues
Unwanted sexual comments, touching or requests
A supervisor giving clear instructions to staff
A guest asking for extra towels for the pool

questions.stem: A guest keeps making rude sexual comments to Shanice, a housekeeper. What should she do?
options: Stay calm, leave the area if needed, and report it at once
Put up with it, since the guest is paying a lot of money
Shout back at the guest so that they know she is upset
Say nothing and simply stop cleaning that villa from now on

questions.stem: A colleague tells you that a supervisor is harassing her. What should you do?
options: Tell everyone at work so that the supervisor is shamed
Tell her to keep quiet so that she does not lose her job
Laugh it off, since supervisors are allowed to joke
Listen, support her, and help her report it properly

questions.stem: Which is an example of unfair discrimination at work?
options: Giving a guest who uses a wheelchair a ground-floor room
Giving a regular guest the room they always ask for
Giving worse service to a guest because of their race
Giving a guest a menu written in their own language

questions.stem: Why should every guest be treated with equal respect?
options: Only guests who pay the most deserve full respect
Respect is only needed when the manager is watching
Every guest deserves good service, whoever they are
Visitors from abroad deserve more respect than locals

questions.stem: You see a co-worker taking food from the villa's store room to take home. What should you do?
options: Ask for some of the food so that you can share it
Report it to your supervisor, as the villa's rules say
Say nothing, since it is none of your business at all
Post about it on social media so that everyone knows

questions.stem: Why should you report a safety or honesty problem, even when a friend is involved?
options: Guests and staff could be harmed if it is kept hidden
Your friend will be given a reward for being caught
You will get your friend's job if they are dismissed
Reporting friends is the quickest way to promotion

questions.stem: You are not sure whether something is ethical. Which is a good question to ask yourself?
options: Will I get caught if I do it when nobody is around?
Will it make my work easier, even if it is wrong?
Has anyone else at work done it before without trouble?
Would I be happy if my manager and family knew of it?

questions.stem: What is the first step when you face an ethical problem at work?
options: Get the facts and work out what the real problem is
Do whatever is quickest, and think about it later
Ask the guest what they would like you to do
Pick whichever choice brings you the most money

questions.stem: What can happen to a worker who breaks the code of conduct?
options: Nothing, because a code of conduct is only advice
A pay rise, for showing that they think for themselves
A warning, suspension or dismissal, as the policy says
Promotion to supervisor, so that they can make the rules

questions.stem: How can one worker's dishonesty harm the whole villa business?
options: It only harms the worker who was dishonest
It makes the villa more popular with guests
It has no effect, as guests never hear of it
Guests stop trusting the villa and stay away

questions.stem: A guest writes a bad online review of the villa. What should staff do?
options: Post angry replies telling the guest that they are wrong
Tell the manager, who can reply politely and fix the issue
Find the guest's home address and complain to them there
Write good reviews under false names to hide the bad one

questions.stem: May you use the villa's car or boat for a personal trip?
options: Yes, if you bring it back before anybody notices
Only with clear permission, as the policy says
Yes, since staff may use anything at the villa
Yes, if you fill the tank before bringing it back

questions.stem: The villa owner's business papers are on the desk in the study. What should you do?
options: Read them to find out how much the villa earns
Take photos of them in case they are needed later
Put them in the bin, since the desk must be clear
Leave them as they are and do not read them

questions.stem: You see a broken step by the pool. What is the professional thing to do?
options: Report it at once and warn people until it is fixed
Leave it, since mending steps is not part of your job
Wait until a guest trips, then report it to the manager
Cover it with a towel so that nobody can see the break

questions.stem: You break a vase while cleaning a guest's villa. What should you do?
options: Hide the pieces and hope nobody notices it has gone
Blame the guest's children when the manager asks
Tell your supervisor at once and fill in a report
Buy a cheap copy and put it in the same place

questions.stem: Two colleagues disagree about how to share the work. What is the professional way to deal with it?
options: Argue it out loudly in front of the guests to settle it
Refuse to work with each other from now on
Complain about each other to the guests
Talk calmly in private, or ask the supervisor to help

questions.stem: Which is a responsible way to treat the environment at the villa?
options: Leave the air conditioning on in empty rooms all day
Save water and power, and sort waste as the villa says
Pour used cooking oil into the garden or the sea
Wash the patio daily with the hose left running

questions.stem: Which of these would be fine to post on your own social media?
options: A photo of a guest asleep on a sun lounger by the pool
The villa's gate code and the times the alarm is off
A team photo from a staff training day, if all agree
A guest's full name and the dates of their stay

questions.stem: Why must staff obey the law as well as the villa's code of conduct?
options: Breaking the law can bring fines or arrest
The law only applies to the villa owner, not to the staff
The code of conduct always takes the place of the law
Laws only matter on days when the police visit the villa

questions.stem: Which is the best way to keep up the standards in the code of conduct?
options: Follow it only on days when the manager is on site
Set a good example, even when no one is watching
Change the rules yourself when they do not suit you
Remind others of the code but do not follow it yourself

theory2.instructions: Section A has 15 short answers (2 marks each). Section B has 10 essay questions (5 marks each): answer each in full sentences. Time allowed: 3 hours 35 minutes. Your answers are saved as you go.

shortAnswers.stem: What one word means keeping private information secret and sharing it only with people who need to know?
What word means being honest and sticking to good moral principles, even when nobody would find out?
What is the word for a worker who reports wrongdoing at work through the proper channels?
What is the word for treating a person unfairly because of their race, religion, sex, age or disability?
What is the word for money a pleased guest gives to staff for good service, on top of the bill?
What do you call money or a favour offered to get someone to do something dishonest or unfair at work?
What one word means arriving on time and keeping to agreed times?
In most villas, who is the first person you report a breach of the code of conduct to?
What is the formal word for being put out of your job for good, for example after stealing?
What word describes the beliefs about right and wrong that guide how a person behaves?
What is the term for guest information such as names, addresses and card numbers, which the law says must be protected?
What is the name of the document that sets out the duties and tasks of a particular job?
What word means doing what you said you would do, so that others can depend on you?
What word means accepting responsibility for your own actions and mistakes?
What is usually the first step in a disciplinary process for a small breach of the rules?

essays.stem: Explain what a code of conduct is and why a villa needs one. Give three examples of rules it might contain.
essays.modelAnswer: A code of conduct is a written set of rules and values that tells staff how they are expected to behave at work. It is usually given to new staff when they start, and they sign to say they have read and understood it. A villa needs one so that every worker knows the standard expected, guests are treated well and kept safe, and the business keeps a good name. It also makes things fair, because the same rules apply to everyone, and staff know what will happen if a rule is broken. Examples of rules are: keep all guest information confidential and never post photos of guests online; do not accept large gifts or commissions without telling the manager; arrive on time in clean uniform; never drink alcohol or take drugs on duty; and report any accident, theft or harassment at once.
markingPoints: Defines a code of conduct as written rules and values for behaviour at work
Explains it sets the standard so guests are served well and kept safe
Explains it protects the villa's good name and treats all staff fairly, with known consequences
Gives at least three suitable rules (confidentiality, gifts, punctuality, no alcohol, reporting)
Mentions it is given to new staff, who read and sign it

essays.stem: Explain why guest confidentiality is important in villa work, and describe four ways staff protect guests' privacy.
essays.modelAnswer: Guests choose a villa because they want comfort, safety and privacy. Some are well-known people, and some simply want to rest without being disturbed. If staff share guest details, guests may be put at risk of theft or unwanted visitors, they lose trust in the villa, and the business can lose guests and even break the law on personal data. Staff protect privacy in several ways. They never tell callers or visitors which villa a guest is in or when the guest is out, and they take messages instead. They keep guest records, passports and card details locked away, and log off computers. They do not talk about guests in public places or with friends and family. They never take or post photos of guests or their belongings. They knock and wait before entering rooms, and they never read guests' papers or screens.
markingPoints: Explains that guests expect privacy and safety, and may be put at risk
Explains the harm to trust, to the business and under the law on personal data
Never gives out guest details to callers or visitors; takes messages
Keeps records and card details secure; does not gossip about guests
No photos or social media posts of guests; respects rooms, papers and screens

essays.stem: Describe how a villa worker shows honesty when handling cash, stock and guests' property.
essays.modelAnswer: With cash, an honest worker counts money carefully, gives the right change and a receipt for every payment, and never borrows from the cash box, even for a short time. If the cash is short or over at the end of the shift, they report it instead of hiding it. With stock, such as food, drinks, toiletries and cleaning supplies, they use only what is needed for the job, record what is used, and never take items home or give them to friends. They report waste, breakages and anything missing. With guests' property, they do not touch, use or move guests' belongings without a reason, and they hand in anything found and record it as lost property. They also fill in time sheets truthfully and follow the villa's rules on tips and gifts. Honesty matters because the villa and its guests must be able to trust every worker.
markingPoints: Cash: counts carefully, gives correct change and receipts, never borrows, reports differences
Stock: uses only what is needed, records use, takes nothing home
Guest property: does not touch or use it; hands in and records lost property
Truthful time sheets and follows the rules on tips and gifts
Explains that honesty builds trust with the villa and its guests

essays.stem: Explain what a conflict of interest is, and describe how you would handle an offer of payment from a taxi driver for sending villa guests to him.
essays.modelAnswer: A conflict of interest is when something that benefits you personally could affect the decisions you make at work, so that you might not act in the best interest of the guest or the villa. For example, if a taxi driver pays me for every guest I send him, I might send guests to him even if his car is not licensed, not safe, or dearer than others. To handle the offer, I would politely tell the driver that I cannot accept it without my manager's approval. I would tell my manager about the offer, because the villa may have rules or approved transport companies. I would only recommend licensed, approved transport, and give guests honest choices. I would never accept money in secret. If the villa does allow commissions, they must be open and recorded, so that guests still get honest advice.
markingPoints: Defines a conflict of interest (personal gain affecting work decisions)
Explains the harm: guests may be sent to unsafe, unlicensed or dearer transport
Politely declines and does not accept money in secret
Tells the manager and follows the villa's policy
Recommends only licensed, approved transport and gives honest choices

essays.stem: Describe what you would do if a guest sexually harassed you or a colleague at work.
essays.modelAnswer: Sexual harassment is any unwanted sexual comment, joke, touching or request. If a guest harassed me, I would stay calm and tell the guest clearly and politely that the behaviour is not acceptable. If I felt unsafe, I would leave the area at once and go to where other staff are. I would not shout or fight back. I would report it straight away to my supervisor or manager, giving the facts: what happened, the date, the time, where it happened and any witnesses, and I would write it down. If a colleague was harassed, I would make sure she was safe, listen to her without judging, and support her to report it, offering to be a witness. I would not spread gossip about it. The villa should then act, for example by keeping staff away from that guest or asking the guest to leave, and the police should be called if there is an assault.
markingPoints: Explains what sexual harassment is
Stays calm, states the behaviour is not acceptable, and leaves if unsafe
Reports promptly to the supervisor with the facts written down
Supports a colleague, listens without judging and keeps it confidential
Knows the villa must act, and police are called for an assault

essays.stem: Describe the steps you would follow to make a good decision when you face an ethical problem at work. Use an example.
essays.modelAnswer: First I would stop and get the facts, so I understand what is really happening. Next I would check the rules: the villa's code of conduct, its policies and the law. Then I would think about who will be affected, such as the guest, my colleagues, the villa and me, and list the choices I have. For each choice I would ask: Is it legal? Is it fair? Would I be happy if my manager and my family knew? If I am still not sure, I ask my supervisor for advice. Then I choose the right action, carry it out, and report or record it if needed. For example, if a guest offered me US$100 to let his friends use the villa pool without paying, I would see that it breaks the villa's rules and is unfair to the owner. I would politely refuse, explain that I cannot allow it, and tell my supervisor.
markingPoints: Gets the facts first
Checks the code of conduct, policies and the law
Thinks about who is affected and lists the choices
Tests each choice (legal, fair, would I be happy if known) and asks for advice when unsure
Acts, reports or records, and gives a suitable worked example

essays.stem: Explain what professional boundaries with guests are, and give examples of how staff keep them.
essays.modelAnswer: Professional boundaries are the limits that keep the relationship between staff and guests friendly but professional. They protect the guest, the worker and the villa. Staff keep boundaries by being warm and helpful but not over-familiar: they use the guest's title and name, and they do not share their personal problems. They do not date guests, go to parties with them, or visit them in their rooms except for work. They do not give out their personal phone numbers, ask for guests' numbers, or follow guests on social media. They do not borrow money from guests, sell things to them privately, or accept large gifts outside the villa's policy. They do not drink alcohol with guests while on duty. If a guest tries to cross a boundary, the worker refuses politely and tells the supervisor.
markingPoints: Defines professional boundaries and why they protect guest, worker and villa
Friendly and helpful but not over-familiar
No dating, socialising, personal phone numbers or social media contact
No borrowing, private selling, or gifts outside the policy; no drinking with guests on duty
Refuses politely and tells the supervisor when a guest crosses a boundary

essays.stem: A colleague is stealing small items from guests' villas. Explain what you should do and why.
essays.modelAnswer: I should not ignore it, even if the items are small and even if the colleague is my friend. Theft from guests is a crime and breaks the code of conduct. Guests trust that their things are safe; if they find items missing they may complain, call the police and stop using the villa, and every worker could be suspected. I should not confront the colleague angrily, search their bag, or tell other staff, as this could cause a fight or spread gossip. Instead, I would write down the facts I saw: what, when and where. Then I would report it privately to my supervisor or manager, following the villa's procedure. If the supervisor is involved, I would go to the next manager or the owner. I would keep the matter confidential and let management investigate. Reporting it protects the guests, my honest colleagues and the villa's good name.
markingPoints: Does not ignore it, even if the items are small or the person is a friend
Explains why: theft is a crime, guests lose trust, everyone may be suspected
Does not confront, search or gossip
Writes down the facts and reports privately through the proper procedure (higher if needed)
Keeps it confidential and lets management investigate

essays.stem: Explain the possible results of breaking the code of conduct for the worker, for the guest and for the villa business.
essays.modelAnswer: For the worker, breaking the code of conduct can lead to a verbal or written warning, suspension, loss of pay, or dismissal, depending on how serious it is and the villa's policy. Serious breaches, such as theft or assault, can lead to arrest and a criminal record, which makes it hard to find another job in tourism. The worker can also lose a good reference and the trust of colleagues. For the guest, a breach can mean poor service, lost or stolen property, loss of privacy, or even danger to their safety, and their holiday is spoiled. For the villa business, a breach can bring complaints, bad online reviews, loss of repeat guests and income, legal claims, and damage to its good name. In tourism, one bad story can travel fast, and it can even harm Jamaica's image as a place to visit.
markingPoints: Worker: warning, suspension or dismissal under the policy
Worker: possible arrest or criminal record, lost reference and trust
Guest: poor service, loss of property or privacy, risk to safety
Villa: complaints, bad reviews, lost guests and income, legal claims
Wider harm to the image of Jamaican tourism

essays.stem: Describe how a villa worker shows professional standards through their appearance, punctuality and behaviour.
essays.modelAnswer: Appearance: the worker wears a clean, pressed uniform and a name badge if one is given, with closed, safe shoes. Hair is neat and tied back for food or cleaning work, nails are short and clean, and jewellery and perfume are kept simple. Good personal hygiene is kept every day. Punctuality: the worker arrives a little before the shift starts, ready to work, and comes back from breaks on time. If they will be late or absent, they call the supervisor as early as possible. They keep to the times agreed with guests, such as breakfast or a tour pick-up. Behaviour: the worker greets guests warmly, speaks politely, listens, and keeps a positive attitude. They keep personal phone use and private chats away from guests, never use bad language, never drink on duty, respect guests' privacy and property, and follow the code of conduct even when no one is watching.
markingPoints: Clean, pressed uniform, safe shoes and neat grooming
Good personal hygiene every day
Arrives early, keeps to break and guest times, and calls ahead if late
Polite, warm, positive behaviour with guests
No phone use or bad language in front of guests, no alcohol on duty, follows the code when unobserved

practical1.title: Produce and present a staff code of conduct poster for a villa
practical1.brief: A villa manager in Ocho Rios has asked your group for a clear, one-page code of conduct for new staff, as a poster. Agree at least ten rules, in plain words, covering honesty, guest confidentiality, gifts and tips, conflicts of interest, harassment, appearance, punctuality, alcohol and drugs, social media, and how to report a problem. Each member writes at least two rules, each with a one-line reason, and the group checks the wording together. Then present the poster to the assessor as if to new staff: every member explains their own rules and answers one question from the assessor. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group, with the finished poster.
materials: Flip-chart or poster paper, markers and rulers
A sample code of conduct or staff handbook from the Centre, if there is one
A phone or tablet for photos
photos: The group's first list of ideas on paper
The draft rules, showing each member's two rules with reasons
The finished poster, readable in one photo
The assessor's question sheet, with each member's answer noted
checklist: Took part in agreeing the list of rules
Wrote at least two clear rules in plain words, each with a correct reason
Rules agree with good practice (confidentiality, honesty, gifts policy, no harassment, safe reporting)
Spoke clearly and confidently when presenting
Listened to others and helped check the wording respectfully
safety: Use markers in a ventilated room and keep the caps on when not in use
Keep walkways clear of paper and bags
Treat every member's ideas with respect; no personal remarks
Do not use real guest or staff names on the poster

practical2.title: Role-play and record ethical situations at a villa
practical2.brief: The assessor gives your group four situation cards, for example: a guest offers cash to let friends use the pool; a caller asks which villa a famous guest is staying in; a housekeeper finds jewellery after a guest checks out; a co-worker is seen taking stock home. For each card, two or three members act out the situation and how a professional worker deals with it, while another member notes what was said. Then the group fills in a short report form for each situation: what happened, the rule or value involved, what was done, and who it was reported to. Share the parts so that every member acts in at least one role play and writes at least one report form. Photograph each stage below and add the photos to the group's practical. Hand in once for the whole group, with the four report forms.
materials: Four situation cards from the assessor
Blank report forms, one for each situation
A simple set: a table, a phone, a lost property book and a room key
Pens, a clipboard, and a phone or tablet for photos
photos: The four situation cards and the group's plan of who plays each part
The four completed report forms laid out together
checklist: Acted in at least one role play and dealt with the situation professionally
Spoke politely and stayed calm, even when the 'guest' or 'colleague' pushed
Named the right rule or value (honesty, confidentiality, gifts policy, reporting)
Chose the right person to report to, and the right way to report
Filled in at least one report form clearly and accurately, with facts only
safety: Role plays use words only: no pushing, grabbing or touching
Use made-up names, never real guests or staff
Any member may stop a role play if they feel uncomfortable
Keep the room tidy and walkways clear
